steps.name: Yato
steps.text: Captain's audio log number two.

steps.name: Yato
steps.text: Current time, 0915 hours. Weather, cloudy. We have returned to the Soubo mountain range, and are currently continuing our advance.

steps.name: Yato
steps.text: Since the last recording, I along with Operator Noir Corne have encountered a series of unexpected situations while executing our mission.

steps.name: Yato
steps.text: We first engaged in combat with an unknown lifeform... a Rathalos. We were not successful in this endeavor.

steps.name: Yato
steps.text: Upon arriving at the village, our usual investigation into the source of the Oripathy outbreak was met with significant resistance from the locals.

steps.name: Yato
steps.text: Their reasons are still unclear, though from the medical tests conducted, it seems that the villagers have been in contact with Originium for an extended period of time.

steps.name: Yato
steps.text: In summing up the clues we've gathered so far, we have determined a course of action: we will continue to track the Rathalos into the forest to try and pinpoint the source of Originium contamination. Progress so far has been poor...

steps.name: Yato
steps.text: Ugh—The thicket here is too dense. Corne, hand me an axe.

steps.name: Yato
steps.text: What did you just hand me? I said to give me an axe, not—what is this...uneven... and squirming...ah!

steps.name: Yato
steps.text: An Originium slug?!

steps.name: Felyne Artisan
steps.text: Originium slug?

steps.name: Yato
steps.text: Why was there one on my hand?

steps.name: Felyne Artisan
steps.text: The slug has no bones... and a very hard carapace, very good! I like it very meowch!

steps.name: Yato
steps.text: Corne—where did you go?

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: Hey mew, take a look. The seeds of this plant burst out with just a touch.

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: They flew so far away, pawbably to extend the range of theirs dispersal... reminds me of a Blastnut.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: This might be related to the Rathalos's whereabouts...Oh! Could it be...

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: I'm pawsitive that is completely unrelated to our search.

steps.name: Yato
steps.text: (Breathes deeply)

steps.name: Yato
steps.text: ...We are currently travelling with some additional companions from another continent that bear some resemblance to Felines.

steps.name: Felyne Artisan
steps.text: That's Felynes to mew!

steps.name: Yato
steps.text: They call themselves Felynes with a Y, and possess information on the Rathalos.

steps.name: Yato
steps.text: With the help of these Felynes and the extensive problem-solving expertise of Rhodes Island Operations Team A4, I believe we will soon unravel this incident.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Yato! This way!

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: No, over here! The Rathalos went this way!

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: But you said it was this way earlier...

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: Those were old tracks, it left new ones here!

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: Hmph! Anyway, just head this way! Mew are as stupid as a Kestodon!

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: What did you say? What's a Kestodon—

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Augh! Who chopped down the tree here?

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: A slow monster that purretty much always charges around and gets stuck in trees!

steps.name: Yato
steps.text: ...We're close to getting to the bottom of this. Recording complete.

steps.name: Yato
steps.text: Corne. Felynes.

steps.name: Yato
steps.text: Listen up, we've been walking for two hours, and have yet to see even a glimpse of the Rathalos.

steps.name: Yato
steps.text: If you'd like to continue your argument, I'll send you both back to that cave to have a nice chat with all the Originium slugs.

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: Smithy, keep your meows down.

steps.name: Felyne Artisan
steps.text: Mrow?

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: Look over there, on the flowers.

steps.name: Felyne Artisan
steps.text: In the underbrush?

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: Undoubtedly, there must be—yes! A whole bunch of tiny, squirming, endemic lifeforms hidden beneath!

steps.name: Felyne Artisan
steps.text: Just a little closer—

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: Hidden within the shadows, danger creeps closer, with the flying insects none the wiser...

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: The concealed predator holds for just a meowment, fur its chance is close at paw! The time is... now!

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: One expels a puff of smoke, and the insects are wobbling, are they about to fall?

steps.name: Felyne Artisan
steps.text: Mrrow... head hurts...

steps.name: Felyne Artisan
steps.text: A—Achoo—

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: Smithy! Look at what you did! Scared them all away!

steps.name: Felyne Artisan
steps.text: Suddenly so sleepy... so many meowterials dancing in the clouds...

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: Even the flying insects dropped from that puff of smoke... could it be one of its properties?

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: I shall note this down... a new kind of endemic lifeform that can cause drowsiness in those affected. Purrphaps it may even be helpful in hunts.

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: Tiny endemic life and flying insects, flying insects and nectar, Meownsters and Hunters... the resemblance is too much to bear.

steps.name: Felyne Artisan
steps.text: Mrrow... just like...

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: Yes, Smithy. I've been noticing this ever since we came here, but while I'm pawsitive that Terra is a totally different world, it shares so many similarities with ours.

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: Whether it be the villagers or creatures I've observed, a closer look has revealed that we share meowch more commonalities than diffurences.

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: Our Ecological Survey in the forest so far has led me to the conclusion that while the endemic life here appears diffurent from the ones we are used to back home, the way things work is exactly the same.

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: Plants, herbivores, carnivores... predator and prey constitute the basis of most biological relationships.

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: The degree of similarity between these two worlds... is simply remeowkable.

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: As I've said befur, our prior knowledge is adequate to understand this world, fur there is no fundamental diffurence.

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: I can also record the Rathalos's activities here up close, and become Terra's top ecological researcher.

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: I'm the purrime scholar after all! Meowhahaha!
To be an ecological researcher here, Originium will definitely be a factor to consider.

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: Originium, mew say? I did hear Noir Corne mention it multipaw times, but I have not whiskered any obvious influence...

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: I don't think it's that meowch of a problem. If you simply take a look at people like Noir Corne, they're pawbably just too dumb to understand how it truly works, purrphaps the rocks have their own special qualities even!

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: However, this forest does indeed raise some concerns in me. It feels like something's missing, but I can't be sure what.

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: What could it pawssibly be...

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: Smithy, what do mew think—

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: Ah, Noir Corne? Why are you here?

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Me? Should I not be?

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: Smithy? Mrow? Where did mew go?

steps.name: Yato
steps.text: If I recall correctly, is that it?

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: I'll go take a look.

steps.name: Yato
steps.text: Careful, don't step on it.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Hey, you're right. Straight from the pages of 'The Originium Slug's Guide to Terran Wildlife'... Vanilla reminded us of this countless times before we left.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: 'Top three creatures to worry about in the forests!' 'An aerial nightmare you definitely want to avoid!'

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Sporting dazzling silver and black feathers and an appearance from the front as dark as a ghost in the night...

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: If you see patches of black and silver feathers on the ground, it means there's a stinkfowl nest nearby.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: And the moment you step into their territory, only one thing awaits you...

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: Yato! Noir Corne! I can't find Smithy anywhere!

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: What? Where did you lose sight of him?

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: We were just meowing about, and he—

steps.name: Yato
steps.text: Corne... did you hear that?

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Yeah, sounds like wings flapping in the sky to me.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: They're getting more intense...

steps.name: Yato
steps.text: Over there.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: S-Should I go take a look?

steps.name: Felyne Artisan
steps.text: Meow!

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Arty! Where have you been?

steps.name: Felyne Artisan
steps.text: Noir Corne! Fur mew!

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: What? This is...

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Wait, don't just skedaddle! Where are you going?

steps.name: Yato
steps.text: Corne... isn't that...?

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: You don't mean—

steps.name: Yato
steps.text: Stinkfowl eggs.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Hey! Arty! Get back here this instant!

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Ah—Don't come any closer, it wasn't me who took your eggs! I'll even put them back for you, okay?

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: I'll return them right now! Don't peck me! Not my horn!

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Agh! It stinks! Blegh—

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Yato! Help me out!

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Arty! No more egg pinching for mew!
From Operator Noir Corne's personal experience:
If you are in the forest and see molted feathers from Stinkfowls marking their territory, never trample upon their nest.
And never, ever touch their eggs.
Otherwise, what greets you is only...
A foul and fierce assault from the sky to be reckoned with.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Did we get away? They're not chasing us, right?

steps.name: Yato
steps.text: They got stopped over there.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: I'm beat...

steps.name: Yato
steps.text: Do you want some water?

steps.name: Yato
steps.text: Wait, don't come any closer to me.

steps.name: Yato
steps.text: Put your shield up so it can block the smell a little... I'll toss the bottle over.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Yato...

steps.name: Yato
steps.text: Corne, I hope you understand that it's best for us to keep our distance for now.

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: Mew stink! Stay away from meow!

steps.name: Felyne Artisan
steps.text: Further!

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: You guys—

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: —Ah!

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: I'm feeling pretty dizzy, is it from all the headpecking earlier?

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: I feel like... the earth is shaking... Did I pass out? Is this a dream?

steps.name: Yato
steps.text: No, that's not it...

steps.name: Yato
steps.text: Get up! Now!

steps.name: Felyne Artisan
steps.text: There's so meowny of them...

steps.name: Felyne Scholar
steps.text: Lots of meownsters are rushing down the mountain!
